issue.title: [Bugfix] Don't report sibling cache hits in n>1 prefill stats
issue.body:
## Overview

**goal:** an `n>1` request reports prefix cache usage the way an `n=1` request does.

**context:** the `n` children share the prompt, so later children hit the kv blocks their sibling just wrote. non-streaming responses took `cached_tokens` from the last child to finish: a cold `n=4` request reported 1,216 of 1,230 prompt tokens as cached (streaming reported 0).

## Claims

- `ParentRequest` keeps the prefill stats (`num_cached_tokens`, `num_cache_creation_tokens`) of the child with the fewest cached tokens, i.e. what was cached before the request. children with no prefill stats (failed before prefill) are skipped.
- the request output reports those stats. per-child prometheus metrics are unchanged (#56361).

## Validation

- `test_parallel_sampling_num_cached_tokens` (new): fails on main (`assert 112 == 0` at 16-token blocks, `64 == 0` at 64), passes here at both.
- `test_parallel_sampling_skips_child_without_prefill_stats` (new): a child that errors before prefill no longer pulls the value to 0.
- a100, llama-3.1-8b, vllm main 4527515cd, cold `/v1/completions`, 2 trials: `cached_tokens` at `n`=2/4/8 is 1216–1264 on main, 0 here. warm `n=4` = warm `n=1` = 1248. chat completions: same. re-checked at cb50988 on 64-token blocks: cold 0 at every `n`, streaming and not; warm `n=4` = warm `n=1` = 1216.
- related engine tests on a100 at cb50988: 8 passed. pre-commit passes.

## Details

- the minimum can undercount only if blocks are evicted between siblings, never overcount. preemption doesn't change it: prefill stats are recorded at first scheduling only.
- not a duplicate: #55120 (multi-prompt requests), #56361 (prometheus metrics).
- ai-assisted (metamate). i reviewed every line and ran the tests.

---

issue.title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Keep vllm-bench warmups and ready check out of the prefix cache
issue.body:
## Overview

**goal:** `vllm-bench` warmups and ready check don't prime the prefix cache for the measured run (rust counterpart of #66701, same bug as #66698).

**context:** warmups and the ready check resend request 0, so the first measured request was a cache hit.

## Claims

- same behavior as #66701: a unique `cache_salt` per warmup and on the ready check; one unsalted warmup retry if every salted warmup fails, with a warning carrying the first error.
- `wait_for_endpoint` takes an optional fallback input, sent only when the server answers the salted probe with a failure (not on connection errors). multi-turn passes none.
- the warmup send loop moved into `send_warmups`.

## Validation

- 5 new tests against a stub server. warmups: distinct salts, other `extra_body` kept; all salted requests rejected → 2 salted then 2 unsalted; one rejected → no retry. ready check (through `run_benchmark`): salted probe then the unsalted run; salted probe rejected → unsalted probe, then the run. each fails when the fix is broken on purpose.
- end to end against a real `vllm serve` (a100, llama-3.1-8b, 1024-token prompts, 3 prompts, `--num-warmups 2`), `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` delta per run: main 1,920 (2,880 with `--ready-check-timeout-sec 30`), this pr 0 (0).
- `cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib`: 241 passed. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean.

## Details

- a non-object `--extra-body` is replaced for warmups: backends only merge objects, and python treats `null` as `{}`.
- will mirror any design change requested on #66701.

issue.title: Importing torchao.prototype.mx_formats initializes CUDA (device capability checked at module level)
issue.body:
### What happens

Importing `torchao.prototype.mx_formats` initializes CUDA in the importing process, even if nothing from torchao is used afterwards.

`torchao/prototype/mx_formats/kernels.py` computes two flags at module level:

- `_triton_kernels_available` (line 454) calls `is_sm_at_least_100()` and, on ROCm, `is_MI350()`
- `_mxfp8_cuda_kernels_available` (line 1016) calls `is_sm_at_least_100()`

`is_sm_at_least_100()` calls `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` and `is_MI350()` calls `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)`. Both run CUDA's lazy init. `prototype/moe_training/config.py:58` does the same through `is_MI300()` in a dataclass field default.

### Why it matters

Other libraries import this path at load time. For example, transformers imports `torchao.prototype.safetensors.safetensors_support` whenever torchao is installed, and `safetensors_utils.py` imports `mx_formats` (transformers issue: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/50540). So in any environment with torchao installed, the process has CUDA initialized before it does anything.

After that, forking a child that uses CUDA fails:

```
RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess. To use CUDA with multiprocessing, you must use the 'spawn' start method
```

We hit this in vLLM's CI when torchao was installed in the shared test image: tests that fork a worker started failing in jobs that never use torchao, on both CUDA and ROCm.

### Reproduce (machine with a GPU)

```python
import torch
import torchao.prototype.mx_formats  # noqa: F401
print(torch.cuda.is_initialized())  # True; False without the import
```

```python
import os
import torch
import torchao.prototype.mx_formats  # noqa: F401

pid = os.fork()
if pid == 0:
    torch.zeros(1, device="cuda")  # raises "Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess"
    os._exit(0)
os.waitpid(pid, 0)
```

### Versions

torchao 0.18.0 (the same code is on `main` today), torch 2.15.

### Suggested fix

Compute these flags on first use instead of at import, e.g. turn them into `functools.cache`d functions, and give the `moe_training` dataclass field a `default_factory`. That keeps `import torchao...` free of device queries.

comment.body: pr: #5087, including that subprocess test (`test_import_does_not_initialize_cuda`). related: #5088 makes plain `import torchao` fork-safe.

issue.title: [Bug]: `vllm bench serve --num-warmups` primes the prefix cache, so the first measured request is a cache hit
issue.body:
### Your current environment

- vllm main at 4527515cd (python, editable), kernels from the 0.33.0 wheel; the warmup code is unchanged on current main (05caae03c)
- torch 2.14.0+cu130, 1x nvidia a100 80gb, llama-3.1-8b-instruct, default `vllm serve` flags (prefix caching on)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`vllm bench serve --num-warmups N` sends `input_requests[0]` N times before the measured run (`vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`, warmup block), and nothing clears the prefix cache afterwards. with prefix caching on (the default):
- the first measured request is served from cache, so its ttft is a cache hit.
- warmups 2..N are cache hits too, so they don't exercise prefill.

repro: prefix cache reset before each run, 2 runs per row:

```
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 32 \
  --ignore-eos --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 7 --num-warmups {0,3}
```

| `--num-warmups` | request 0 ttft | other requests, median ttft | reported mean ttft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 348 / 353 ms | 329 / 332 ms | 331 / 333 ms |
| 3 | 67 / 81 ms | 334 / 327 ms | 307 / 302 ms |

server counters agree: with 100 prompts × 1024 tokens and 4 warmups, `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` rose by 4,032 = 4 × 1,008 (warmups 2-4 plus measured request 0).

the bias is 1 request out of `num_prompts`: it skews min and mean ttft, most visibly in short latency runs.

fix options:
1. send each warmup with a unique `cache_salt`. warmups then do full prefills and never match measured requests; no server flag needed, but `cache_salt` is vllm-only.
2. `POST /reset_prefix_cache` after warmup (needs `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`; `vllm bench sweep` already resets between runs).

i can send a pr for either.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body: thanks @luyixiao95. i filed this to fix it myself, so i will take it, with the same approach: a unique `cache_salt` per warmup. pr today.

issue.title: [RFC / Performance] How LLM Agent Context Compaction Collapses Automatic Prefix Caching (APC)
issue.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Many long-horizon LLM Agent frameworks perform context compaction (summarization) to prevent context window overflow. In our production runs (~81k context), we observed that compaction caused a severe prefill stall (TTFT stalled at 206.9s), collapsing vLLM's Automatic Prefix Caching (APC) hit rate down to 10.1%.

Root Cause:
Agent frameworks often strip older archive checkpoints from the prompt to "keep the window lean". This drops an early message and shifts all subsequent tokens, causing APC prefix matching to fail right after the system prompt (token 8,886). 73k tokens had to undergo full re-prefill.

The Proposal & Benchmark:
By ensuring the compaction request's message prefix is token-identical to normal conversation turns, APC hit rate immediately recovered to 99.6%:
- Cache Hit Rate: 10.1% -> 99.6%
- Cached Tokens: 8,192 -> 144,165
- Re-prefilled Tokens: 72,986 -> 627 (116x reduction)
- TTFT: 206.9s -> 3.1s (66x faster)

We propose adding guidelines/warnings in vLLM docs regarding APC-friendly prompt construction for Agent builders.

### Alternatives

Explicit cache control breakpoints can help, but keeping the prefix token-identical in the request builder is the cleanest, zero-overhead solution.

### Additional context

Full methodology, de-identified logs, and 2-second model-free reproduction script:
https://github.com/yansu202511/cache-alignment-findings

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body: i'd like to take the docs part: a section in the automatic prefix caching docs on keeping the prompt prefix token-identical across agent turns, plus a repro script that sends the same conversation to `vllm serve` twice (once with an early message dropped, once with the prefix kept identical) and reports the prefix cache hit rate for each. @yansu202511 are you planning to write this yourself? if not, i'll send a pr.

issue.title: repeated runs hit the prefix cache, so the reported median can be a warm-cache number
issue.body:
`lib/run_vllm_bench.sh` runs every repetition on the same server with the same prompts (`random`, default seed 0), and nothing clears the prefix cache in between. when a config's prompts fit in the kv cache, runs 2-3 are served from cache and the reported median is a cached run.

repro: `lib/run_vllm_bench.sh` at `bc1b8e0`, unmodified, native runtime. 1x a100 80gb, vllm 0.33.0, llama-3.1-8b-instruct, kv cache 457k tokens.

| config | run | prefix cache hit | median ttft | req/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| random 1024/256, 200 prompts, concurrency 64 (fits) | 1 | 0.5% | 1648 ms | 6.05 |
| | 2 | 98.4% | 232 ms | 9.74 |
| | 3 | 98.4% | 232 ms | 9.71 |
| | reported | | 232 ms | 9.71 |
| random 8192/1024, 256 prompts, concurrency 128 (doesn't fit) | 1-3 | ≤0.9% | ~116 s | 0.56 |

a nightly config is affected when `num_prompts × input_len` fits in that deployment's kv cache. to check: `GPU KV cache size` in the server log, or run 1 vs run 2 ttft in `bench-<name>-run-<n>.json`.

fix options:
1. `POST /reset_prefix_cache` before each run (needs `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`). keeps the same prompts across runs and nights.
2. a different `--seed` per run. no server change; prompts differ per run.

i can send a pr for either.
